actual: Neither fault point exists yet: the supervisor and the cancel command ran to the end (the pty-driven command printed 'run <id>: cancelled; 1 decision withdrawn' and exited 0 instead of being killed; the live supervisor had already moved the run to cancelled where the test expects it still running), so every kill-point test fails on its first assertion about the kill
semanticAssessment: The failures are assertion failures about the kill (the command was killed, the supervisor died before the transition), never load, import or syntax errors: the fixtures start real live and blocked S-17 runs, the pseudo-terminal harness ran the real cancel command, and the ordering, empty, terminal and adjacency tests of the same file pass against the Task 1 and 2 code, as regression guards of the edges.
